werk/blink-182-cheshire-cat.text:
Cheshire Cat is the debut album by the American band Blink-182, who at the time were still simply called Blink. It was released on 17 February 1995 on the San Diego label Cargo Music. The trio, guitarist Tom DeLonge, bassist Mark Hoppus and drummer Scott Raynor, had formed in 1992 and had made three demos that won Cargo over. The album was recorded quickly, mostly at Westbeach Recorders in Los Angeles, with producer Otis Barthoulameu and few overdubs.

The sixteen songs combine fast power chords and melodic hooks with silly jokes, alongside a handful of more serious songs about relationships and insecurity. M+M's and Wasting Time were released as singles, while Carousel became a fan favourite. The album grew steadily, thanks to advertising in skate magazines and local radio. When an Irish band of the same name threatened legal action, the trio added 182 to their name.
werk/blink-182-cheshire-cat.listen: Listen to Carousel and notice the tempo, the simple power chords and the melody that still rises above them.

werk/blink-182-dude-ranch.text:
Dude Ranch is the second studio album by Blink-182 and was released on 17 June 1997. It came out on Cargo Music, with MCA Records handling distribution. After Cheshire Cat the band had toured extensively, including on the 1996 Warped Tour, and as a result had attracted the interest of major labels. It is the last record to feature all three original members: drummer Scott Raynor was fired in 1998.

The band chose producer Mark Trombino for his work in the emerging emo scene. He pushed for tighter, more disciplined recordings. The songs, largely written on the road, blend the band's familiar goofy humour with themes such as growing up and relationships. The sleeve plays with absurd cowboy imagery. Dammit became a hit on modern rock radio and won over new listeners. The record received mostly good reviews.
werk/blink-182-dude-ranch.listen: Listen to Dammit and notice how tightly the band plays, and how well the melody suits the fast tempo.

werk/blink-182-take-off-your-pants-and-j.text:
After the enormous success of 1999's Enema of the State, the band had to make a follow-up in a short space of time. Recording ran from December 2000 to March 2001 with the same producer, Jerry Finn, mostly in San Diego. The label MCA put pressure on the deadline, and the three members disagreed about the direction. During the writing, Travis Barker was given the status of official member.

When their manager complained that there was no summery hit on the album, Mark Hoppus wrote The Rock Show in ten minutes, and Tom DeLonge wrote First Date. Both became hits, as did Stay Together for the Kids. Take Off Your Pants and Jacket became the first punk album to reach number one in the United States. Critics praised its take on teenage themes; others saw precisely there its weakness.
werk/blink-182-take-off-your-pants-and-j.listen: Listen to The Rock Show, which according to Mark Hoppus was written in ten minutes, and notice how simple and singalong it is.

werk/blondie-autoamerican.text:
Autoamerican was released in November 1980 and was Blondie's fifth album. The group recorded in Los Angeles, at the insistence of producer Mike Chapman, while the sleeve was made in New York. It was a clear change of course. The opener Europa is a dramatic instrumental overture with orchestra, over which Debbie Harry speaks a lyric about car culture.

The group explored many styles. Here's Looking at You and Faces sound like jazz and blues. The Tide Is High is a cover of a Jamaican rocksteady song by the Paragons from 1967. Rapture combines funk, rock, jazz and the new rap, and became the first rap song to reach number one in the United States. Follow Me is a cover from the musical Camelot. According to drummer Clem Burke, the record label heard no hit, yet the album produced two number ones. The intended title was Coca Cola, but the company rejected the idea.
werk/blondie-autoamerican.listen: Listen to Rapture and notice how funk, rock and rap come together in a single song.

werk/blondie-eat-to-the-beat.text:
Eat to the Beat was released on 28 September 1979 on Chrysalis, as Blondie's fourth album. It followed Parallel Lines, with which the group had already moved towards rock-tinged pop. Mike Chapman produced. He later wrote that the group wanted to try everything, that there was a lot of arguing in the studio and that drugs became a problem.

The album continues the pop course, with excursions into rock, disco, punk, reggae and funk, and even a lullaby. Atomic and The Hardest Part blend disco with rock. Dreaming, Union City Blue and Atomic were released as singles in Great Britain. The album was also released as one of the first video albums, with short films by David Mallet. Critics were divided: some saw a second-rate rehash of Parallel Lines, others found it fresh and varied. In the United Kingdom the record reached number one.
werk/blondie-eat-to-the-beat.listen: Listen to Atomic and notice how disco and rock meet here.

werk/blondie-parallel-lines.text:
After their second album Plastic Letters, Blondie switched from producer Richard Gottehrer to the Australian Mike Chapman. In June 1978 the band recorded their third album at the Record Plant in New York. The atmosphere in the studio was tense. Chapman rehearsed a great deal with the band members and carefully guided Debbie Harry in particular through her vocals. Many songs were not yet finished when recording began. The lyrics of Sunday Girl and One Way or Another, among others, only took shape during the sessions. The album was finished in six weeks, whereas the record company had allowed six months.

The record is pop, not punk. Chapman himself said he was making a pop album. Heart of Glass is the only disco piece, with nervous keyboards. The album reached number one in the United Kingdom and marked the breakthrough in the United States, where Heart of Glass became their first number one.
werk/blondie-parallel-lines.listen: Listen to Heart of Glass and notice the keyboards darting nervously through the song. What does that do to the disco rhythm?

werk/blondie-plastic-letters.text:
Plastic Letters is Blondie's second album, released in February 1978 by Chrysalis Records. Richard Gottehrer produced it, for the last time. During the recording the band were still bound to Private Stock. Bassist Gary Valentine had just left the group, and Frank Infante played guitar and bass as a session musician. Chris Stein played lead guitar. The sleeve design with Debbie Harry's pink dress was by Anya Phillips.

The album was a success mainly in Europe. Denis, a cover of Denise by Randy and the Rainbows, reached number 2 in the United Kingdom, and (I'm Always Touched By Your) Presence, Dear, written by Valentine, reached number ten. The album itself reached number 10 and went platinum in the United Kingdom. The Globe and Mail wrote that the band's hardness was softened by quirky arrangements. The 2001 reissue also includes the first demo of what would later become Heart of Glass.
werk/blondie-plastic-letters.listen: Listen to Denis and notice how a pop song from 1963 is turned into a playful song by the band, with Debbie Harry's vocals up front.

werk/blur-13.text:
13 was released on 15 March 1999 and is Blur's sixth album. It moves further away from Britpop, towards art rock and electronica, and is darker and more personal, strongly influenced by Damon Albarn's break-up with Justine Frischmann. Recording ran from June to October 1998 in London and Reykjavik. For the first time the album was produced not by Stephen Street but by William Orbit, whom the band chose after his remix of Movin' On.

The atmosphere in the studio was tense and members stayed away from the sessions. Orbit saw a struggle between Albarn's experimental direction and Graham Coxon's punk direction. Bugman sounds industrial and the album closes with Optigan I, made with an optical organ. It reached number 1 in England, produced three singles and was nominated for the Mercury Prize. Reviews were largely favourable.
werk/blur-13.listen: Listen to the instrumental closing track Optigan I and notice the sound of the Optigan, an optical organ.

werk/blur-blur.text:
After the success of Parklife, The Great Escape brought a setback. Oasis outsold them commercially and the band came to be seen as a fake middle-class group. The mood within the group was tense. Guitarist Graham Coxon was listening to American indie rock such as Pavement and proposed a different course. Damon Albarn felt the same was needed and asked producer Stephen Street for a barer sound. Recording began in June 1996 in London and continued in Reykjavik in Iceland. For the first time the group jammed together in the studio, which Coxon found exciting.

The album was released on 10 February 1997 on Food Records. It sounds more aggressive and more emotional, and the lyrics are more personal. The label and the music press feared that the young fans would drop away, but the album and the first single Beetlebum went to number one in England. Song 2 made the band bigger in America than ever before. Most critics praised the change of style and Albarn's lyrics.
werk/blur-blur.listen: Listen to Song 2 and notice how raw and short it is, compared with the Britpop the band had made in the preceding years.

werk/blur-leisure.text:
Blur released this debut album on 26 August 1991 on Food Records. The band took their lead from the Madchester and shoegaze that were popular in the British indie scene at the time, very different from the Britpop they would later come to define. It was also the start of their collaboration with producer Stephen Street, who produced most of the twelve tracks.

The album contains the first three singles: She's So High, There's No Other Way and Bang. Sing, a song the band had already recorded as a demo in 1989, later ended up on the soundtrack of Trainspotting. The British press responded with mixed reviews, but the album reached number 7 in the UK chart and went gold. Damon Albarn later called it an unpleasant experience and the band played little of it live. Only There's No Other Way and She's So High remained regular fixtures in the setlist.
werk/blur-leisure.listen: Listen to There's No Other Way and notice how the band builds a pop song here with a danceable, somewhat languid rhythm from the baggy years.

werk/blur-modern-life-is-rubbish.text:
After the success of Leisure, Blur fell out of favour in 1992. The band was in debt, came back disillusioned from a failed American tour and was told that the record company Food would drop them. Damon Albarn pushed for a new course: back to the British guitar pop of groups such as the Kinks and the Small Faces. A first attempt with producer Andy Partridge failed. Stephen Street finished the album, and on Christmas Day Albarn wrote For Tomorrow to keep the record company happy.

The sound is melodic and rich, with brass, strings and backing vocals. Advert is punk, Sunday Sunday sounds like vaudeville. The music press was full of praise and the album reached number 15. It is regarded as one of the defining records of Britpop.
werk/blur-modern-life-is-rubbish.listen: Listen to For Tomorrow and notice the brass and the backing vocals that make the song sound broader than an ordinary guitar band.

werk/blur-parklife.text:
Blur had sold only modestly with Modern Life Is Rubbish and were short of money. So in August 1993 the group quickly went back into the studio, at Maison Rouge, with producer Stephen Street. Recording went smoothly, except for This Is a Low. Label owner David Balfe was not pleased and said it was a mistake. Shortly afterwards he sold Food Records to EMI. Years earlier Damon Albarn had promised that the third record would make the group the English band of the nineties.

Albarn called the record a loosely connected concept album about the travels of a lager drinker. The styles vary widely: synth-pop in Girls and Boys, an instrumental waltz in The Debt Collector, punk in Bank Holiday and strange space sounds in Far Out. The sleeve shows greyhound racing. Parklife was well received, topped the British chart and is regarded as the Britpop record.
werk/blur-parklife.listen: Listen to The Debt Collector and notice how the track, without vocals, sounds like a little waltz among the other songs.

werk/boards-of-canada-geogaddi.text:
Geogaddi is the second studio album by the Scottish duo Boards of Canada, released on 18 February 2002 on Warp Records. Between 1999 and 2001 the two recorded more than ninety tracks in their studio Hexagon Sun in the Pentland Hills, and chose 22 that fitted the mood they were after. They wanted to make a large, psychedelic whole, darker than their debut Music Has the Right to Children.

The sound consists of heavily processed samples and analogue sounds, with acoustic instruments and flutes that have been heavily treated. Inspiration came from the Incredible String Band and the film The Wicker Man. The themes are numerology, paganism and religious cults, with hidden messages and reversed sounds. Warp sent no promotional copies to journalists, but held listening sessions in churches. The critical response was very positive: the record appeared in many best-of-2002 lists and is regarded as a defining work of intelligent dance music.
werk/boards-of-canada-geogaddi.listen: Listen to 1969 and notice the sounds and the atmosphere: does it feel warm or menacing, or both?

werk/boards-of-canada-music-has-the-righ.text:
Music Has the Right to Children is the debut album by Boards of Canada, the Scottish brothers Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin. It was released in 1998 on Warp and Skam Records. They made it in their own studio Hexagon Sun in the Pentland Hills, after two earlier EPs, Twoism and Hi Scores. Both labels wanted to release the record, so they released it together. The brothers used samplers, deliberately detuned old synthesizers, drum machines and tape recorders.

The sound is warm, grainy and nostalgic. There are samples from Sesame Street and from American and Canadian television programmes of the seventies, often with distorted voices. In Rue the Whirl, birdsong ended up on the tape by accident because the window was open. The brothers let it stay. Critics responded with praise and the album is regarded as a milestone of electronic music. It inspired later artists.
werk/boards-of-canada-music-has-the-righ.listen: Listen to the birdsong in Rue the Whirl. It ended up on the recording by accident and stayed there all the same.

werk/bob-dylan-blonde-on-blonde.text:
In October 1965 Bob Dylan began work in New York on his seventh album, with his backing band the Hawks. Months of sessions yielded almost nothing, apart from One of Us Must Know (Sooner or Later). At the suggestion of producer Bob Johnston, the recording moved to Nashville, where in February and March, together with Al Kooper and Robbie Robertson and a group of top session musicians, he recorded all the other songs.

Blonde on Blonde completed a trilogy of rock albums, after Bringing It All Back Home and Highway 61 Revisited. It was released as a double album, one of the first in rock. The music sounds grand; one critic described the lyrics as a mixture of the visionary and the everyday. Rainy Day Women #12 & 35 and I Want You became hits. Just Like a Woman and Visions of Johanna are regarded as his finest compositions. Critics often count the album among the best of all time.
werk/bob-dylan-blonde-on-blonde.listen: Listen to the lyrics in Visions of Johanna, which are long and vivid, and to how subdued the band plays beneath them.

werk/bob-dylan-blood-on-the-tracks.text:
After a tour with The Band in 1974, Bob Dylan began work on new songs, written after lessons with the painter Norman Raeben, who by his own account changed his view of time. He re-signed with Columbia and in September 1974 began recording at A & R Studios in New York, under producer Phil Ramone. He chose bare acoustic arrangements and worked spontaneously. When his brother felt the record sounded too bare, he re-recorded five songs in late December at Sound 80 in Minneapolis.

The songs are often read as an account of a marriage in crisis, although he denies they are autobiographical. Tangled Up In Blue jumps through time, and Idiot Wind is a fierce reckoning. The first reviews were mixed, but later the record came to be regarded by critics and fans as one of this singer's best and as a fixture on lists of the greatest albums ever.
werk/bob-dylan-blood-on-the-tracks.listen: Listen to Tangled Up In Blue and notice how the story jumps back and forth in time while the acoustic guitar sets the pace.

werk/bob-dylan-bringing-it-all-back-home.text:
In the summer of 1964 Bob Dylan spent hours in Woodstock writing his lyrics, which grew ever more surreal. Then he met the Beatles, and together with producer Tom Wilson he sought a blend of rock and folk. The first session, on 13 January 1965 in New York, was still entirely acoustic, but the result was almost entirely rejected. In the end the record was released in April 1965 on Columbia, as Dylan's first album with electric instruments.

On the first side an electric rock 'n' roll band plays; the second side consists mainly of acoustic songs. Dylan left the protest music of his earlier records behind for more complex, surreal lyrics. The album caused controversy and divided the folk scene. Subterranean Homesick Blues became his first single on the American charts. It was also his first LP in the American top 10 and later that spring went to number one in Great Britain. Several magazines name it one of the best albums of all time.
werk/bob-dylan-bringing-it-all-back-home.listen: Listen to Subterranean Homesick Blues and notice how the electric band drives the lyrics onward, then compare that with the acoustic mood of Mr. Tambourine Man.

werk/bob-dylan-desire.text:
This album was released in January 1976, between two legs of the Rolling Thunder Revue, and is one of Bob Dylan's most collective records. The idea of having a band of his own came in the summer of 1975, when he saw Patti Smith and her group play in New York. He met the violinist Scarlet Rivera on the street and asked her to play with him. He wrote most of the lyrics together with Jacques Levy, and Emmylou Harris sang along.

The record consists of long narrative songs. Hurricane, the opener, protests against the conviction of the boxer Rubin Carter, whom the song says was innocent. Joey lasts eleven minutes and caused an uproar because it was said to glorify the gangster Joey Gallo. The album followed Blood on the Tracks, was well received and was very successful in England and America.
werk/bob-dylan-desire.listen: Listen to Hurricane and notice the violinist, whose playing drives the boxer's story forward.

werk/bob-dylan-highway-61-revisited.text:
In May 1965 Bob Dylan came back exhausted from a tour of England and even considered giving up singing. He wrote Like a Rolling Stone. The song was recorded on 15 and 16 June in Columbia's Studio A, under producer Tom Wilson. Guitarist Michael Bloomfield played on it, and Al Kooper came up with an organ riff, even though he had never played electric organ before. The rest of the record followed from 29 July to 4 August under Bob Johnston.

The title refers to the highway that connects Duluth, his birthplace, with cities such as Memphis and New Orleans and with the region of the Delta blues. A rock band plays on every track, except the closing piece Desolation Row, an eleven-minute ballad. Critics praise the way the record combines driving, blues-based music with poetic lyrics. Michael Gray argued that the sixties in a sense began with this record.
werk/bob-dylan-highway-61-revisited.listen: Listen to Like a Rolling Stone and notice the organ sound that Al Kooper came up with at the last moment, and how it pushes the song forward.

werk/bob-dylan-john-wesley-harding.text:
John Wesley Harding was released in late December 1967 on Columbia Records, produced by Bob Johnston. It was Bob Dylan's first album after three records of abstract, blues-influenced rock. It was recorded in Nashville in the autumn of 1967, in less than twelve hours spread over three sessions. While he was making the Basement Tapes with the Band, Dylan chose different songs for this record.

The accompaniment is remarkably sparse: only drummer Kenneth Buttrey and bassist Charlie McCoy join Dylan's guitar, harmonica and voice. In a year when psychedelia dominated pop culture, the album was seen as contrarian. Dylan asked Columbia for no publicity and no single was released. Even so it sold well and its reputation grew. All Along the Watchtower became one of his best-known songs after Jimi Hendrix released it in 1968.
werk/bob-dylan-john-wesley-harding.listen: Listen to All Along the Watchtower and notice how little you hear: guitar, harmonica, bass and drums. Can you hear how that bare accompaniment makes the song menacing?

werk/bob-dylan-love-and-theft.text:
Love and Theft was released on 11 September 2001 and is Bob Dylan's thirty-first studio album. It was his first record with the band he was touring with at the time, joined by keyboard player Augie Meyers. The twelve tracks were recorded in May 2001 in twelve days at Clinton Recording in Manhattan. According to engineer Chris Shaw, he let go of arrangements quickly and would try a song in another key, at another tempo or in another style until it fitted.

The sound draws on old American music: jump blues, slow blues, rockabilly, Tin Pan Alley and Country Swing. The characters are crooks, gamblers and drifters. High Water (for Charley Patton) paints a portrait of Southern history, and Sugar Baby closes as a long, sombre ballad with plenty of echo. Critics received it even more enthusiastically than the record before. According to Dylan himself, it is about business, politics and war, and perhaps a little love.
werk/bob-dylan-love-and-theft.listen: Listen to Tweedle Dee & Tweedle Dum and notice the galloping drums and the sharp guitar riffs beneath the story of two drifters.

werk/bob-dylan-modern-times.text:
Modern Times was released on 29 August 2006 and is Bob Dylan's thirty-second studio album. After Time Out of Mind and Love and Theft, it was the third acclaimed record in a row. He produced it himself under the pseudonym Jack Frost. He recorded it with his touring band in New York, after rehearsals in Poughkeepsie. According to engineer Chris Shaw, the sessions lasted about a month, slightly longer than for the previous record.

The music stays close to blues, rockabilly and the balladry of the pre-rock 'n' roll era. A debate arose because he had used choruses and arrangements from older songs without crediting them. Rollin' and Tumblin' is a blues standard that Muddy Waters also played; apart from the first line, the lyrics are new. The album entered at number 1 in the United States, for the first time since Desire in 1976. It won Grammys, topped Rolling Stone's list for 2006 and inspired Elton John.
werk/bob-dylan-modern-times.listen: Listen to Rollin' and Tumblin' and try to hear that this is an old blues standard for which Dylan wrote new lyrics.

werk/bob-dylan-nashville-skyline.text:
Johnny Cash had already said in 1965 that he would like to make a Nashville album with Bob Dylan. It took until 1969 before that happened. Nashville Skyline built on the rustic style of John Wesley Harding, but went completely into country music. The songs are simple and homely, and he sings in a soft country voice that listeners had not heard from him before. He had temporarily given up smoking.

Cash sings along on Girl from the North Country. The album was released on 9 April 1969, promotion ran partly through Cash's television show, and it became one of his best-selling records. Critics mostly reacted positively. Paul Nelson wrote in Rolling Stone that the album made a deep, human statement about being happy. Others felt something was missing. Kris Kristofferson later said that Dylan opened all the doors in Nashville and brought a new audience there, so that the country scene was never the same again.
werk/bob-dylan-nashville-skyline.listen: Listen to the two voices of Dylan and Johnny Cash in Girl from the North Country. Notice how different Dylan sounds here from on his earlier records.

werk/bob-dylan-new-morning.text:
Four months after the notorious Self Portrait, Bob Dylan came out with New Morning. It looked like a hasty reaction to the criticism, but a large part of the album was already finished when Self Portrait was released. Recording took place in May and June 1970 at Columbia Studios in New York. Al Kooper took part as co-producer, but the final mix went badly, because he kept changing his mind.

Some of the songs he wrote for the play Scratch, a musical version of The Devil and Daniel Webster. These became New Morning and Father of Night, among others. He withdrew from the project, but according to Kooper the songs formed the beginning of the album. After the controversial previous record, it was above all his familiar, somewhat nasal voice that came as a relief. The press and the fans were far more positive. The album reached number seven in the United States. If Not for You also became an international hit for Olivia Newton-John.
werk/bob-dylan-new-morning.listen: Listen to Dylan's voice in If Not for You, which on this album sounds like it did on his earlier records. Notice how simply the song is constructed.

werk/bob-dylan-rough-and-rowdy-ways.text:
Bob Dylan recorded this record in January and February 2020 at Sound City Studios in Los Angeles. It was his first album of his own songs since Tempest in 2012, after three albums of old pop standards. Recording followed directly on from a tour that many critics said included his best performances in years. The Never Ending Tour band played on it, joined by Blake Mills and Fiona Apple, among others.

It is one of his most varied albums. Acoustic folk, such as I Contain Multitudes, stands alongside electric blues numbers such as False Prophet. I've Made Up My Mind to Give Myself to You is a ballad. Murder Most Foul lasts almost seventeen minutes and contains a long string of song titles. The lyrics are dense and full of references, about art, religion, death and political assassinations. Critics were unanimous in their praise, and Murder Most Foul became his first song to top an American Billboard chart.
werk/bob-dylan-rough-and-rowdy-ways.listen: In Murder Most Foul, listen to the piano, played by Fiona Apple and Alan Pasqua. Also notice the long string of titles of other songs that passes by in the lyrics.

werk/bob-dylan-tempest.text:
Bob Dylan recorded this album between January and March 2012 at Groove Masters Studios in Santa Monica, Jackson Browne's studio. He produced it himself, under the pseudonym Jack Frost. His own touring band played on it, joined by David Hidalgo of Los Lobos, who contributed accordion and tres. Scott Litt was the engineer and recorded the band with old omnidirectional microphones in a single room. All the songs are by Dylan himself, except Duquesne Whistle, which he wrote with Robert Hunter.

It sounds traditional and the lyrics are dark. Duquesne Whistle and Early Roman Kings were released as singles. The video for Duquesne Whistle at first looks like a light comedy in the style of Charlie Chaplin, but according to Rolling Stone it takes a shockingly dark turn. Because of the title, some thought this would be his last album, after Shakespeare's last play, but Dylan dismissed that. Critics responded with praise.
werk/bob-dylan-tempest.listen: Listen to Duquesne Whistle and notice the old-fashioned, almost jazzy and traditional sound of the band.

werk/bob-dylan-the-basement-tapes.text:
After his motorcycle accident in July 1966, Bob Dylan withdrew to Woodstock. In 1967 he recorded more than a hundred songs there with the future members of The Band, first in his house and then in the basement of the house known as Big Pink. There were original songs, covers and traditional numbers. The style was more intimate than on his earlier albums and leaned on American folk music, with humour, but also themes such as betrayal and the search for redemption.

The recordings circulated for years as bootlegs. Only in 1975 did an official release appear on Columbia: sixteen songs by Dylan and The Band from 1967, supplemented with eight songs by The Band alone, and with overdubs. The record was received with praise. Some critics did wonder why well-known songs from 1967 were missing and why recordings by The Band that had not been made in Woodstock were included.
werk/bob-dylan-the-basement-tapes.listen: Listen to Tears of Rage. Richard Manuel wrote the music for a lyric that Dylan gave him, so notice how the vocals and the accompaniment form a single whole.

werk/bob-dylan-the-times-they-are-a-chan.text:
For his third album Bob Dylan wrote all the songs himself. His first two records also contained covers. Recording began in August 1963 in Columbia's Studio A in New York, with Tom Wilson as producer. After a two-month break, sessions followed in October, and Restless Farewell came last, on 31 October. The record was released in February 1964.

The songs are sparse in design and deal with racism, poverty and social change. He wrote the title song deliberately as a song with a purpose. Ballad of Hollis Brown tells a grim story about a poor farmer in South Dakota, and Only a Pawn in Their Game refers to the murder of Medgar Evers. Critics found the record less varied and less humorous than his previous work. Even so it reached number 20 on the American chart and later number 4 in the United Kingdom.
werk/bob-dylan-the-times-they-are-a-chan.listen: Listen to The Times They Are A-Changin' and notice the short verses that pile up hypnotically.

werk/bob-dylan-time-out-of-mind.text:
After Under the Red Sky in 1990, Bob Dylan had gone for years without releasing new songs of his own, only two albums of folk covers and a live record. In the winter of 1996 he wrote a new batch of songs on his farm in Minnesota. Producer Daniel Lanois, with whom he had earlier made Oh Mercy, recorded them with him at Criteria Studio in Miami. The official sessions began in January 1997. He wanted a sound influenced by early blues musicians such as Charley Patton and Little Walter.

The album sounds atmospheric, thanks to carefully placed microphones and a distinctive mix. Many fans and critics saw the record as his comeback. It won three Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year in 1998. He himself was not satisfied with the sound, and he produced his later albums himself.
werk/bob-dylan-time-out-of-mind.listen: Listen to Love Sick and notice how the singer sounds: according to producer Lanois, the voice was treated like a harmonica being overdriven through a small guitar amplifier.

werk/bob-marley-en-the-wailers-exodus.text:
On 3 December 1976 an attempt was made on Bob Marley's life in Jamaica. He survived, played the Smile Jamaica concert two days later all the same, and then left for London. There the group recorded this album. The title was already settled before the title song existed. He wrote it in answer to the election slogan of Prime Minister Michael Manley, and it became a number one in Jamaica.

The sound is relaxed, with pulsing bass, piano and guitar, and in the title song also trumpets. The lyrics are more direct than on earlier records and deal with change, religious politics and love. The first half opens with Natural Mystic, while the second half revolves around love and staying faithful. Jamming, Waiting in Vain, One Love and Three Little Birds became major international hits. The record brought the singer international fame, and Time named it the best album of the twentieth century in 1999.
werk/bob-marley-en-the-wailers-exodus.listen: Listen to Natural Mystic and notice the slow tempo and how the song gradually builds.

werk/bob-marley-en-the-wailers-survival.text:
Survival is the eleventh album by Bob Marley and the Wailers and was released in 1979. Its theme is markedly militant. Some critics think this was partly due to the criticism of the relaxed mood of the previous record, Kaya. The title was at first going to be Black Survival, but it was shortened to avoid misunderstandings. Neville Garrick designed the sleeve with 48 African flags and an image of the slave ship Brookes in the background.

In Africa Unite, Marley calls for Pan-African solidarity. Zimbabwe is a hymn to what was then still white-ruled Rhodesia and was played at the Zimbabwe independence celebrations in 1980. In South Africa the album was partly censored because of apartheid. The group produced the record themselves, together with Alex Sadkin.
werk/bob-marley-en-the-wailers-survival.listen: Listen to Africa Unite and notice how the lyrics argue for Pan-African unity.

werk/bon-iver-22-a-million.text:
The songs on this third album took shape between 2012 and 2016. Justin Vernon recorded it in his own studio, April Base, in Eau Claire, Wisconsin. It is a clear change of course: the folk of the early days gives way to electronic music, with many samples, synthesizers and wind instruments. Many sounds were created and processed with a Teenage Engineering OP-1 and with a harmonizer designed for the band. The lyrics are largely about Bon Iver's growing fame and how Vernon's relationship to the world changed as a result.

The record had its premiere at Vernon's own festival Eaux Claires. Numerous samples are worked in: 22 Over Soon uses a piece of Mahalia Jackson, 10 Death Breast a song by Stevie Nicks, and 00000 Million a song by Fionn Regan. Critics praised the idiosyncratic sound and the colourful lyrics. Pitchfork and Rolling Stone later placed the album on their lists of the best albums of the decade.
werk/bon-iver-22-a-million.listen: Listen to 22 (OVER S∞∞N) and notice how the sampled gospel fragment by Mahalia Jackson sounds through the electronic textures.

werk/bon-iver-bon-iver-bon-iver.text:
For the second album Justin Vernon brought in other musicians, such as bass saxophonist Colin Stetson and pedal steel guitarist Greg Leisz. He built up the record himself, but he let the guests change the sound. Recording took place at April Base Studios in Fall Creek, Wisconsin, a converted veterinary clinic that Vernon and his brother had bought in 2008, close to the house where he grew up. The album was seen as a new direction compared with the debut.

Each song stands for a place, and that gives the record its theme. Perth was the first song Vernon wrote. Minnesota, WI combines fingerpicked guitars, double bass drums and a distorted bass saxophone. Holocene is named after a bar in Portland and after a geological epoch. Beth / Rest, full of brass, closes the album and is the song Vernon was proudest of. The critical response was full of praise, and the album won a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album.
werk/bon-iver-bon-iver-bon-iver.listen: Listen to Minnesota, WI and try to pick apart the fingerpicked guitars, the double bass drums and the distorted bass saxophone.

werk/bon-iver-for-emma-forever-ago.text:
Justin Vernon was living in Raleigh, North Carolina, when he fell ill, first with pneumonia and then with mononucleosis and a liver infection. His band fell apart and he became frustrated with his writing and his life. He drove to his father's remote hunting cabin in Wisconsin, hoping to be alone. There, between late 2006 and early 2007, he recorded the album. He abandoned his old way of working and first wrote melodies without words, to which he later added lyrics. He hunted his own food and spent a lot of time alone.

His folk songs have heavy choral arrangements, with his falsetto and horns. The lyrics are about lost love and mediocrity. He released the album himself in July 2007 and signed to Jagjaguwar later that year. Skinny Love became the best-known single. Critics were full of praise and the album appeared on dozens of year-end lists. It grew into a major success for an independent label.
werk/bon-iver-for-emma-forever-ago.listen: Listen to Skinny Love and notice how Vernon's falsetto and the simple accompaniment create an intimate, lonely atmosphere.

werk/bon-iver-i-i.text:
Bon Iver saw i,i as the fourth and last season of a cycle. For Emma, Forever Ago was winter, Bon Iver, Bon Iver spring and 22, A Million summer. This album was autumn. Frontman Justin Vernon called it the most mature and complete record. It was recorded over a long period at April Base in Wisconsin and finished at Sonic Ranch in Texas. James Blake, Aaron Dessner, Bruce Hornsby and Moses Sumney, among others, contributed. It was released on 8 August 2019, one song every hour.

The sound combines elements of the earlier albums: acoustic guitars, horns, piano, synthesizers and layered voices, with a more sparing use of electronics than on 22, A Million. Most critics were full of praise. The album received Grammy nominations, including for Album of the Year.
werk/bon-iver-i-i.listen: In iMi, listen to how acoustic sounds and electronics run into one another. Also notice the voices, which lie over one another in layers.

werk/bon-jovi-7800-fahrenheit.text:
7800° Fahrenheit is the second studio album by the American rock band Bon Jovi. It was released on 27 March 1985 on Mercury Records. The title refers to the supposed melting point of rock and was meant to promise American hot rock. The record was made in six weeks, between January and March 1985, at the Warehouse Studios in Philadelphia, with producer Lance Quinn. It was their last collaboration.

On this album four band members co-wrote the songs. Secret Dreams is the only song with a writing credit for drummer Tico Torres. Tokyo Road opens with the Japanese folk song Sakura Sakura. Only Lonely and In and Out of Love reached the Billboard Hot 100. The band themselves were unhappy with the sound and later all but disowned the album, although it is a fan favourite.
werk/bon-jovi-7800-fahrenheit.listen: Listen to the beginning of Tokyo Road and recognise the Japanese folk melody Sakura Sakura with which the song opens.

werk/bon-jovi-keep-the-faith.text:
After the tour for New Jersey the band took a break. Jon Bon Jovi wrote the music for Young Guns II, Richie Sambora made a solo record and the singer fired his manager in order to take more responsibility himself. In 1992 the group spent seven months working on the fifth album at Little Mountain Sound Studios in Vancouver, led by producer Bob Rock. Bruce Fairbairn, who had produced earlier records, was too busy with Aerosmith.

Of thirty songs written, fourteen made it onto the album. The music became more serious than before, and the band deliberately ignored what had changed in rock. Dry County and Bed of Roses grew out of a summer in which the singer rode anonymously through Arizona on his motorcycle. The album reached number five on the American chart and number one in Great Britain. It is also the last studio record with all five original members.
werk/bon-jovi-keep-the-faith.listen: Listen to Bed of Roses, a song that grew out of a summer on the motorcycle, and notice how personal the lyrics sound.

werk/bonobo-black-sands.text:
Black Sands is the fourth album by the English producer Bonobo. It was released on 29 March 2010. All the songs are by him, and he also plays a large part of the instruments, including piano, bass guitar, Fender Rhodes, harmonium, harp, xylophone and music box. Guests complement this: singer Andreya Triana on three tracks, as well as violins, flute, saxophone, clarinet, trombone and trumpet.

The sleeve carries a photograph of Derwentwater in the north of England. Tracks from the album can be found in films and series: All In Forms in a 2012 film, Kong in House of Cards and Black Sands as the title song of the French film The Measure of a Man. In England the record went silver.
werk/bonobo-black-sands.listen: Listen to Eyesdown and notice how Andreya Triana's vocals relate to the instruments around them.

werk/bonobo-days-to-come.text:
Days to Come is the third album by Bonobo, the artist name of Simon Green. It was released on 2 October 2006 on the independent label Ninja Tune, in a standard version and in a limited edition with a second disc full of instrumental versions of the vocal tracks. Green wrote and played six tracks entirely himself.

On other tracks, Bajka and Fink, among others, sing. Ketto turned up in the series Skins and in an advert for the Citroën C4 Picasso, and If You Stayed Over was heard in an episode of Lost. In 2006 the album was chosen as Album of the Year on Gilles Peterson's show on BBC Radio 1.
werk/bonobo-days-to-come.listen: Listen to If You Stayed Over and notice how Fink's voice is used on an electronic record.

werk/bonobo-dial-m-for-monkey.text:
Dial 'M' for Monkey is the second studio album by the British electronic artist Bonobo. It was released on 17 June 2003 on the label Ninja Tune. He wrote and played all the tracks himself. The album contains nine pieces, from Noctuary to Light Pattern.

Flutter was the only single from the record, with a Four Tet Mix of Pick Up and Something (Longer) as B-sides. The CD came with a short animated film by Conkerco, which goes with one of the tracks. The album became known through the use of its music elsewhere. Flutter and Pick Up were heard in the snowboarding game SSX on Tour. Flutter was later heard in TV series and in adverts on Film4, and Wayward Bob was in the film Gumball 3000: The Movie. In 2012 the record received a double silver certification from the Independent Music Companies Association for at least 40,000 copies sold in Europe.
werk/bonobo-dial-m-for-monkey.listen: Listen to Flutter, the song that was released as a single, and notice all the sounds you can hear.

werk/bootsy-collins-fresh-outta-p-univer.text:
After his years as P-Funk's bassist, Bootsy Collins released the studio album Fresh Outta 'P' University in 1997. It was first released on WEA/Black Culture in Europe and Japan, and then in the United States on Private I, distributed by Mercury. Many guests take part, including MC Lyte, Rodney O, D Meka, Thomas D and Smudo, and Fatboy Slim. From the P-Funk family, Bernie Worrell, Fred Wesley and Garry Shider, among others, play on it.

The album came out in several editions. The European deluxe version consisted of two CDs in a sleeve that folds open into six panels, which together spell the word Bootsy. The Japanese New Edition contained remixes of Party Lick-A-Ble's and Do the Freak. The track listing also differs by version: the European one contains Home-Of-Da-Freaks, for example, the American one Shiggy Wiggy.
werk/bootsy-collins-fresh-outta-p-univer.listen: Listen to Do the Freak and notice the role of the bass in the groove, the instrument of the man who made the album.

werk/bootsy-collins-the-one-giveth-the-c.text:
This Bootsy Collins album was released on 28 April 1982 and was his last for Warner Bros. Records. It was also the first record he produced entirely himself. Only Shine-O-Mite (Rag Popping) he made together with George Clinton, who also co-wrote the song with him.

Collins himself played bass, guitar, drums and keyboards. Many people from the world of P-Funk and the Rubber Band took part, including the horn players Fred Wesley and Maceo Parker, guitarist Phelps Collins and the group Godmoma. Two songs were released as singles: Take a Lickin' and Keep On Kickin and Shine-O-Mite. The single versions differ from the album versions and never appeared on CD. The album was reissued in Japan in 1990 and later in Europe. In 2007 an edition followed via Rhino Records.
werk/bootsy-collins-the-one-giveth-the-c.listen: Listen to Take a Lickin' and Keep On Kickin and notice how the bass and the rhythm guitar push the song forward.

werk/bootsy-collins-ultra-wave.text:
Ultra Wave was released in November 1980 on Warner Bros. Records and was the fifth album by funk musician Bootsy Collins. It was the first record to appear under his own name alone, whereas the earlier albums had been by Bootsy's Rubber Band. George Clinton and Collins produced the album together, except for three tracks, Is That My Song, Fat Cat and Sound Crack, which Collins did alone. Recording ran at the same time as that of Sweat Band, a project led by Collins. Like the previous record, this is a more experimental and more progressive album.

Well-known names took part in the recording, including the horn players Fred Wesley and Maceo Parker. A Canadian newspaper called Fat Cat a vicious dance number and Sacred Flower beautiful, full and deep in the background. In 2007 the album was reissued via Rhino Records.
werk/bootsy-collins-ultra-wave.listen: Listen to Sacred Flower and notice the full, deep sounds in the background, with the solo on the lyricon.

werk/boudewijn-de-groot-welterusten-mijn.text: In 1966 Boudewijn de Groot sang Welterusten mijnheer de president, a mocking lullaby addressed to the American president Johnson about the war in Vietnam. The lyrics were written by Lennaert Nijgh. It was Bob Dylan in a Dutch guise: a protest song in their own language, with an acoustic guitar. De Groot and Nijgh showed that in Dutch you could make serious songs that appealed to young people.
werk/boudewijn-de-groot-welterusten-mijn.listen: Hear the soft, rocking melody, like that of a lullaby, beneath a sharp lyric about bombs and war.

werk/boy-george-boyfriend.text:
Boyfriend was released in April 1989 on Virgin, Boy George's third solo album. It came only six months after Tense Nervous Headache, which Virgin had not wanted to release in the United Kingdom. At the suggestion of Sharon Heyward, head of the black music department, the American producers Gene Griffin and Teddy Riley flew to London. They recorded four songs of which the singer was not happy. To recoup the money, Virgin released the single Don't Take My Mind on a Trip, which reached number 5 on the American R&B chart.

Virgin then put this album together: the four songs by Riley and Griffin on the first side, two unreleased songs on the second, plus Girlfriend from the soundtrack of Slaves of New York and the protest single No Clause 28. The sleeve of the previous album was reused, with a different photograph from the same session. The album did not chart anywhere.
werk/boy-george-boyfriend.listen: Listen to Don't Take My Mind on a Trip and notice the beats of Teddy Riley, the producer of the first four songs.

werk/boy-george-high-hat.text:
High Hat was released in 1989 and is a compilation of tracks from Boy George's second and third solo records in the United Kingdom and Europe, Tense Nervous Headache and Boyfriend. Together those albums had eighteen tracks. Tense Nervous Headache was withdrawn in Great Britain shortly after the first single owing to lack of interest, even though the year before he had topped the charts with Everything I Own. High Hat remained the only place to find his songs from 1988 and 1989.

Half of the ten tracks were singles that had little success, such as Don't Cry, Whisper and You Found Another Guy. Don't Take My Mind on a Trip became a club hit in Canada and the United States. The album reached number 126 there. AllMusic felt that as a soloist Boy George was aiming at a smaller audience, with barely disguised confessions over new jack swing rhythms.
werk/boy-george-high-hat.listen: Listen to Don't Take My Mind on a Trip and notice the rhythm, which is clearly meant for the dance floor.

werk/boy-george-sold.text:
Sold was the first solo album by the British singer Boy George and was released in 1987 on Virgin Records. It appeared after the break-up of his band Culture Club in 1986 and his recovery from a drug addiction. The best-known song is his cover of Everything I Own, which reached number one in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Norway and the top ten in several other countries.

Three more singles followed: Keep Me in Mind, the title track Sold and To Be Reborn. In Europe the album did well, in the United States much less so. There it got no further than number 145 on the Billboard 200. The reviews were good.
werk/boy-george-sold.listen: Listen to Everything I Own and notice how calm and sensitive his voice sounds in this song.

werk/boy-george-tense-nervous-headache.text:
During the first recording sessions, Boy George says, he did not know whether he wanted to be Prince, Bowie or Roy Orbison. Tense Nervous Headache, released on Virgin in October 1988, was his second solo album. The title refers to a British television advert for Anadin. He began with Bobby Z., a Prince associate, but also drew inspiration from acid house and garage, as on his protest single No Clause 28. Teddy Riley recorded four new jack swing songs, with which the singer was unhappy and which were left off the album.

Sales were disappointing. The first single Don't Cry stalled at number 60 on the British chart, after which Virgin withdrew the album in the United Kingdom. In Europe it was released. Later the singer called the record self-indulgent and muddled. In March 1989 Virgin released a new album, Boyfriend, with the songs by Riley.
werk/boy-george-tense-nervous-headache.listen: Listen to Don't Cry and notice the singing: the voice sounds here like that of a crooner, in the style of Roy Orbison.

werk/brad-mehldau-elegiac-cycle.text:
Elegiac Cycle is a solo piano album by Brad Mehldau, released in 1999 by Warner Bros. and produced by himself. For its design he drew inspiration from James Joyce's Ulysses. The album is built cyclically, with a theme that opens the record and returns at the end, just as Odysseus's journey was a circle.

A musical effect also comes from Joyce. In Memory's Tricks, Mehldau silently holds down the keys of a motif with one hand and improvises other lines with the other. The motif then sounds softly on in the vibrations of the soundboard. The pieces are all his own and bear titles such as Elegy for William Burroughs and Allen Ginsberg and Goodbye Storyteller. In 2011 an edition containing all the notes of the album was published in France.
werk/brad-mehldau-elegiac-cycle.listen: Listen to Memory's Tricks and notice how a motif keeps sounding in the background while other lines are played over it.

werk/brad-mehldau-highway-rider.text:
Highway Rider was released in 2010 on Nonesuch Records as a double album. It was Brad Mehldau's second collaboration with producer Jon Brion, after Largo. The pianist plays here with his regular trio, bassist Larry Grenadier and drummer Jeff Ballard, but also with saxophonist Joshua Redman and drummer Matt Chamberlain.

The album is conceived on a broader scale than an ordinary piano trio album. A chamber orchestra conducted by Dan Coleman plays on some of the tracks. Besides piano, there are also pump organ, orchestra bells and a Yamaha CS-80, an analogue synthesizer. The result is a long series of pieces in which jazz, orchestral sounds and studio colours flow into one another.
werk/brad-mehldau-highway-rider.listen: In Highway Rider, listen to the sound of the synthesizer next to the piano. Notice how that analogue colour makes the piece sound different from an ordinary jazz trio.

werk/brad-mehldau-introducing-brad-mehld.text:
This album was released in 1995 on Warner Bros. and has nine tracks: a mix of standards and original compositions, produced by Matt Pierson. The pianist plays with two different trios. On the first five tracks Larry Grenadier plays bass and Jorge Rossy drums, on the last four Christian McBride and Brian Blade. In 2023 he wrote that you hear two records in one: his own voice, coloured by musicians who already had a sound of their own.

Alongside his own work such as Angst, Young Werther, London Blues and Say Goodbye there are pieces by Rodgers and Hammerstein, John Coltrane with Countdown, Duke Ellington with Prelude to a Kiss and Cole Porter with From This Moment On. AllMusic gave four stars and called it a good start to what was to become a prolific career.
werk/brad-mehldau-introducing-brad-mehld.listen: Listen to Countdown, a composition by John Coltrane and, at just over four minutes, the shortest track on the album, and notice what the bass and drums do around the piano melody.

werk/brad-mehldau-largo.text:
Largo was released in 2002 on Warner Bros. and is an album by pianist and composer Brad Mehldau. It is a departure from his earlier straight-ahead jazz records. Instead it sounds more experimental and more pop-influenced, with many session musicians. Jon Brion produced and was his main collaborator, but the pianist wrote all the arrangements himself.

The music includes chamber-music-like woodwinds and brass, and percussion with hip-hop and drum-and-bass rhythms. He also plays electric keyboards. According to the reviewers, his piano remains the centre. His playing stays a little ominous and sad, but he plays more lightly and his melodies and harmonies are simpler than before. The Guardian gave the record four stars. According to AllMusic, it shows how open the pianist is to new sounds, although his playing remains intelligent and somewhat cerebral. In 2023 the album was released on vinyl for the first time.
werk/brad-mehldau-largo.listen: Listen to When It Rains and notice how the woodwinds and the piano sound together: what do the woodwinds add?

werk/brainpower-dansplaat.text: In May 2002 the Amsterdam rapper Brainpower released Dansplaat. The song spent four weeks at number 1 in the Top 40 and also topped the chart in Flanders. Brainpower was the first Dutch-language solo rapper to reach number 1 in both countries. In the lyrics he mentions all sorts of things from that time, from Wim Kok to Tekken 3. With this, Nederhop had truly become pop music.
werk/brainpower-dansplaat.listen: Hear the fast, playful raps and notice the references to names and things from 2002.

werk/brand-new-heavies-brother-sister.text:
Brother Sister by the Brand New Heavies was released on 22 March 1994 on Delicious Vinyl. It was the last record by singer N'Dea Davenport with the acid jazz and funk band: she left to finish her own solo album and returned ten years later. Spend Some Time spent two weeks at number two on the American dance chart. Midnight at the Oasis, a cover of Maria Muldaur, became popular in England, but is not on the American version.

According to Billboard, the record weaves traditional jazz threads through a warm fabric of funk and R&B, with Davenport's alto in the leading role. NME praised the opener Have a Good Time, a groove without much singing. Music Week found the album professional but somewhat lukewarm. Music & Media compared it with the swinging work of the Average White Band.
werk/brand-new-heavies-brother-sister.listen: In Have a Good Time, listen to the saxophone in the style of Maceo Parker, which together with the rhythm section carries the groove of this largely instrumental track.

werk/brand-new-heavies-shelter.text:
The Brand New Heavies released Shelter in 1997 on Delicious Vinyl. It is the only album on which singer and songwriter Siedah Garrett can be heard as a permanent band member. She joined the group in 1996 and left in early 1998 to focus on her own songwriting.

The album produced four singles. Sometimes reached number 11 on the British chart. A remix with rap by Q-Tip later gained a special reputation: according to Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, J Dilla's remix was the inspiration for Got 'til It's Gone by Janet Jackson. The cover of You've Got a Friend, a song by Carole King, became the group's only British top 10 hit, at number 9. You Are the Universe and Shelter reached numbers 21 and 31. In the United States the cover was not on the first pressings.
werk/brand-new-heavies-shelter.listen: Listen to You've Got a Friend, a song by Carole King, and notice how the band makes its own version of it.
